strategy_summary: Use the semigroup tree but track each genus-h semigroup by its label e(Λ), the number of effective generators. First rewrite N(h+1) as the weighted count Σ e·n_h(e), where n_h(e) counts genus-h semigroups with exactly e effective generators. Then prove a local lower bound: if a parent has e effective generators and s strong ones, then the sum of the labels of all its children is at least e(e−1)/2+s. Summing over all parents gives a global lower bound for N(h+2). The theorem is reduced to one explicit bottleneck inequality involving the distribution n_h(e) and the total strong-generator count S(h).
